response.rationale: The fat signal on MRI and TTE finding of LHIS strongly favor a lipomatous lesion. The SVC obstruction explains the progressive dyspnea and exercise-induced BP drop. D1 is most likely given the known LHIS and its potential to extend into the SVC; D2 is a close alternative but less likely due to the presence of LHIS on TTE. Time/scope: symptoms over 9 months and absence of acute features favor a benign process.
